subject: Future Tech
title: Stellarators: The Twisted Cousin
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Stellarators: The Twisted Cousin.

hook.text: A stellarator looks like a pretzel designed by a supercomputer.

buildup.text: Tokamaks need a current running through the plasma, which causes instabilities. Stellarators avoid this entirely.

discovery.text: Germany's Wendelstein 7-X is the world's largest stellarator. It ran for 8 minutes of continuous plasma in 2023.

twist.text: Stellarators are harder to design and build. Their complex twisted magnets were impossible before modern supercomputers.

climax.text: If stellarators work at scale, they could run continuously—no pulsing, no disruptions. True steady-state fusion.

punchline.text: Harder to build, easier to run. The long game.

quiz.question: What advantage does a stellarator have over a tokamak?
options: No plasma current means fewer instabilities
